newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling tends weaker against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling tends weaker against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling traded weaker against the dollar on Monday in the face of renewed importer demand, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 56.12 against the dollar from 56.05 on Friday. On the pound, it was posted at an average of 87.74 from 87.54 on Friday.
"The shilling closed the week weaker against the dollar in the face of renewed importer demand as panic buying swept the market," a dealer said.

"Dollar demand also arose as players covered spot their unhedged forward dollar sales that were maturing," she said. "Due to the relatively high premiums, the players did not mind buying expensive dollars as they were short at above 57 level."
Another dealer added: "The market closed at 56.15/35 from the open at 56.05/15. The market should move lower this week and probably stabilise at around 56.10/20."
Dealers said overnight money market rates shot up to 25 percent levels and above as the treasury bills auction mopped up all liquidity in the market.
